properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 11 at 7:34AM CDT until September 11 at 8:15AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out
20 NM...
Coastal waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS out 20 NM...
Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound...

At 734 AM CDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 8 nm southeast of Pensacola Beach to 8 nm southwest of
Fort Walton Liberty Ship Reef, moving northeast at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Mary Esther, Fort Walton Beach, Navarre Beach, East Santa Rosa Sound,
West Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Beach, Oriskany Reef, and Okaloosa
Pier.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 9:46PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From Sunday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Sunday
morning and continue rising to 12.2 feet Sunday evening.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.2
feet on 11/24/1997.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon EDT.

properties.areaDesc: St. Andrews Bay Waterways; Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out 20 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 11 at 6:47AM CDT until September 11 at 8:15AM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
St. Andrews Bay Waterways...

* Until 815 AM CDT.

* At 647 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 9 nm southeast of Santa Rosa Beach, moving
northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Panama City Beach, Laguna Beach, Santa Rosa Beach, Sandestin,
Miramar Beach, and Mexico Beach.
properties.instruction:

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 11 at 8:21AM EDT until September 11 at 10:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by prior excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northern Jackson County in southeastern Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 819 AM EDT, Emergency management reported lingering high water
across portions of the warned area from prior heavy rainfall last
evening and early this morning. Flooding is already occurring.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Jackson, Wellston, Coalton and Byer.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.
